summary: In his harbor office, Merchant Paine paid Kael four times his fare to take a passenger called Vex out into the Strait rather than across it, with no witness on either bank, and Kael took the purse.

states.c1: Descending the stairs from Paine's office into the harbor air, the purse in his hand, committed to a night crossing he has already been paid to betray
states.c3: Still in his harbor-window office, hands folded, having got the agreement he arranged the room to get

facts: Kael is a ferryman and the only ferryman on the Strait; there is no other.
Paine's office has harbor windows and sits above a stair that descends to the harbor.
Two miles west of the harbor the mist begins; beyond it the law of the shore does not reach.
The far shore of the Strait is invisible from the water.
Kael has worked the Strait thirty years and has not lost one passenger.
Paine paid Kael four times his usual fare, in a purse drawn from his desk drawer.
The crossing is set for tonight, on the tide.
The passenger is one person, called Vex: lean, in dark clothes, carrying a bundle of papers and nothing else.
Paine claims the papers, and the person carrying them, belong to him.
Paine's instruction is that the passenger be carried out into the Strait, not across, with no witness on either bank and no boat but Kael's.
Paine wears a ring on his finger.
The compact of the ferry is that the passenger is told the fare and the weather and nothing more.
Kael took the purse.

summary: Kael stowed the purse and took the Glass Ferry out through the harbor mouth into the mist, where Orin discovered that the silent passenger, Vex, was bleeding onto the deck from a bound wound they claimed would hold for the three hours to the far shore.

states.c1: At the tiller, past the harbor mouth with no turning back, the bribe locked in the cabin locker, now knowing his passenger is bleeding and that turning back would deliver a corpse he would have to explain; he has said nothing of the purse and has not decided.
states.c2: Sitting at the foot of the mast in dark clothes with a bundle of documents under one arm, wound exposed and bleeding into a pool on the deck, outwardly composed, having named themselves and stated they can last three hours to the sanctuary.
states.c4: Shaken after being the one to spot the blood, his early-finished rigging work done, still awaiting Kael's orders.

facts: Orin had the lines coiled and the sail ready before Kael reached the slip
Orin asked whether the tide was slack or turning, and whether to reef the sail before or after going out; Kael answered "After"
Kael put the purse in the cabin locker without looking at it
The passenger was already aboard before Kael arrived, having come down the quay and boarded without asking permission
The passenger sat at the foot of the mast with a small bundle of documents under one arm, wearing dark clothes
The passenger gave their name as Vex and nothing more
Kael took the tiller and the boat, the Glass Ferry, left the dock; the harbor mouth passed and mist closed behind them, hiding the near shore
Vex did not move for the first half hour of the crossing
Orin was the first to notice Vex was sitting in liquid, and identified it as not water
A slick black pool of blood spread from where Vex sat, stretching toward the scupper with the boat's roll
Vex claimed the wound is bound and will hold to the far shore
Vex claimed there are people at the sanctuary who can close it
Vex claimed the crossing would take three hours and that they can last three hours
Kael asked what would happen if he turned back; Vex answered that he would be carrying a corpse into the harbor and would have to explain it
The purse in the locker belongs to a man who paid Kael four times over to never reach the far shore

summary: Adrift in the mist beyond the harbor mouth, Kael refused Vex's plea to be carried to the far shore until the purse in the locker reminded him what Paine had paid him for, and he put the bow onto the long line for the far sand.

states.c1: Committed, against his own caution and against Paine's payment, to carrying Vex the full crossing to the far shore, and prepared to bear whatever it costs him on the other side.
states.c2: Still bleeding at the foot of the mast, having won the passage they argued for, and told to bind the wound tighter.

facts: The narration states the boat carries two men, Kael and Vex, and names no one else aboard on this page.
The boat passed the harbor mouth and the mist closed over it, taking the shore from sight.
Vex is seated at the foot of the mast with a dark pool beneath them and is bleeding on the deck.
Vex claims Kael has looked over his shoulder four times since the mist took the mole.
Vex claims Paine has four men on the quay, and that they are there to ensure Vex is never found.
Vex repeats the figure of three hours for the crossing and says they said it before and meant it.
Vex claims the far shore is the only place on this water where they are alive tomorrow, and that Kael is the only man who can put them there.
Kael states there is no turning back in the Strait, and that the water decides that, not him.
Kael has spent thirty years with his hands on this tiller, and merchants, nobles and fugitives have stepped off his prow.
A purse is in the locker of the boat and knocks once during the crossing.
The narration states Kael was paid a fare four times over, and that Paine paid him to be something he has never once been.

summary: Vex argued that the near shore meant their death either way, and Kael answered by setting the tiller for the deep channel and committing to the far crossing.

states.c1: Kael, tempted to turn back and weighing the purse against thirty years, chose to go forward and steered for the deep channel, accepting what the choice would cost him.
states.c2: Vex, wounded and holding the bundle of documents dry under one arm, laid out the case against returning and pressed Kael forward, betraying pain only for a half second.

facts: Three people are aboard the boat on this page: Kael, Vex and Orin.
Orin is forward at the bow with his back to the cabin, and has stayed there since he coiled the last of the lines before the mist took the shore; he does nothing on this page.
Vex has sat at the foot of the mast since the harbor mouth.
Vex keeps the bundle of documents dry under one arm; the deck beneath them is wet.
Kael is at the tiller.
Kael took four times his fare for this crossing.
The rule of the Strait is that there is no turning once the current has you.
Vex claims Paine has men on the near quay who have been there since dark.
Vex claims that if the boat returns with them alive, those men will kill them on the sand, and if it returns with them dead, the men will pay Kael and forget him.
Vex restates their earlier figure of three hours.
A purse is in the locker and knocks once during the scene.
After Vex's argument, Kael said 'Then forward' and set the tiller for the deep channel, where the rocks are.
flag_reason: TR-08: the page call emitted commentary before the prose; retries spent, page accepted flagged
repair_reason: continuity: page 3 said two men aboard where the ledger and page 2 put three

summary: An hour out of the harbor the Glass Ferry hit crossed water at the Strait's heart, and Kael steered the channel by feel while Vex caught Orin from a fall, roped him to the deck and hauled the sheet with him until the boat came through into calm swells with the smell of sand close ahead.

states.c1: Kael is at the tiller, unshaken, having taken the ferry through the crossed water by feel without once looking at the rocks; he has just told Orin and Vex to hold and is running on long slow swells toward the far shore.
states.c2: Vex is kneeling and braced on the wet deck, still holding Orin, having kept the bundle of documents clear under one arm throughout; they gave Orin the order that saved him and added their weight to the sheet.
states.c4: Orin is shaken and still shaking, bruised from going down hard against the cabin after losing his footing on the wet oak, roped round the waist, still holding the rope, having obeyed Kael's order without asking why for the first time.

facts: The Glass Ferry has been running this crossing for fifty years.
The water changed roughly one hour after the ferry left the harbor mouth, placing this page about one hour into the voyage.
Before the change the ferry had been carried out of the harbor mouth on long easy swells.

The boat came through the rough water: she shuddered from prow to stern, heeled, and took green water over the rail that swept the deck ankle-deep; the page reports no damage, leak or breakage, but does not state that the hull is sound.
The ferry's deck is oak.
The rough water was short, crossed and angry, caused by the rocks at the Strait's heart, which lay to starboard and broke water white.
Mist was present throughout, limiting sight of the rocks to sound.
A navigable seam of deep water runs between the rocks and the shoal; Kael found that channel by feel when he was younger than Orin is now, and has been finding it ever since.
Kael did not look at the rocks, and the narration states he has never needed to look at them.
Present on this page: Kael at the tiller, Vex on deck with the bundle of documents, Orin working the sheet. Merchant Paine does not appear.
Vex kept the bundle of documents with them and clear of the water during the rough passage.
After the crossing the swells were long, slow and almost gentle, and the mist carried the smell of sand from close ahead.
Orin was still holding the rope and Vex was still holding Orin at the page's end.

summary: Orin heard water coming up through the boards, Kael found the unreachable breach along the turn of the bilge, said it could not be stopped, refused the two-hour return leg, set Orin bailing only to buy time, took the tiller back from Vex and put the prow at the far shore.

states.c1: Kael knows the hull is holed beyond reach and the boat is lost; he has refused to turn back, set Orin to bail for time only, taken the tiller back from Vex and is steering for the far shore, outwardly unchanged.
states.c2: Vex held the tiller on Kael's order without correcting, asked whether the breach could be stopped and was told no, and has now surrendered the tiller back to Kael.
states.c4: Orin, who found the leak lying flat with his ear to the deck, has been sent for the bailing bucket and told the boat is not being saved.

facts: The breach is along the turn of the bilge, low and long, where it cannot be seen or reached from inside the boat.
Kael states the breach cannot be stopped.
Kael judges the boat will stay afloat about another hour, maybe more, and that he can put her anywhere he chooses within that hour.
Kael judges the return leg to be two hours against the current, which would sink the boat halfway, and refuses it; he also notes men have been waiting on the near quay since dark.
At the end of the page Kael holds the tiller, with the prow set at the far shore.
Orin discovered the water first, lying flat on deck with his ear a handspan from the boards, and identified it as rising from below rather than spray.
Kael ordered Orin to bail not to save the boat but to buy time.
The rocks caused the damage; one plank or beam of the hull has opened.
The boat already handles heavier and slower coming round than before.
The boat has crossed this water for fifty years without ever sinking, and Kael inherited her.
The harbor Kael left at the turn of the tide lies behind them; sand he can smell but not see lies ahead.
Mist is close and white, with no visibility.

summary: Kael ran the sinking Glass Ferry onto the far shore, admitted to Vex that Paine had paid him and that he had carried them across regardless, and stood watching the boat go under after Vex climbed the path into the mist.

states.c1: Standing motionless on the far-shore sand, having confirmed Paine's payment aloud and delivered Vex anyway, watching the Glass Ferry sink after thirty years of crossings.
states.c2: Ashore and unharmed enough to walk, the bundle of documents still held against the bound wound, gone up the narrow path into the mist with no witness on either bank.
states.c4: Silent at the bailing until the hull grounded, then setting the bucket down without being told, having held back the question on his face.

facts: Water came in through the boards faster than Orin could bail it out.
Kael ordered Orin to keep bailing not to save the boat but to keep her nose up another hundred yards.
The mist opened on the far shore all at once, showing rock, steep beach and a black line of hills.
Kael laid the tiller over and let the last swell carry the boat in; the prow struck sand.
Vex stood in the bow holding the bundle of documents against the bound wound.
Vex stated 'Paine paid you' and Kael answered 'He did.'
Vex said 'And you brought me anyway' and Kael answered 'I did.'
Vex went over the rail into knee-deep shallows, climbed the rocky beach, found the narrow path and walked into the mist, unobserved from either bank.
Kael did not move from the grounded boat; Orin set the bucket down without being told.
The Glass Ferry settled by the stern, water rising past the cabin door, sill, window and roof until it was level and still; the boat sank after thirty years on the Strait.
